name: noisy_agent_stream
description: Simulates a realistic agent stream where high-value decisions are mixed with noise: tool echoes, status confirmations, ambient chat, and boilerplate acknowledgments. 24 events total — 8 signal (4 topics × 2 events) and 16 noise (4 noise categories × 4 events each). The current HeuristicWriteDecider admits all 24 because every event passes the length and dedup checks. This scenario exists to measure whether noise dilutes consolidation quality — if the consolidator mixes signal with noise into impure facts, there's a case for a ContentTypePriorDecider that filters by content type before admission. Built 2026-04-10 to test A-MAC's claim that content-type prior is the most influential factor in memory admission.

events.text: We decided to migrate from API keys to OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for all mobile clients because API keys were leaking through client-side JavaScript bundles in production.
OAuth 2.0 PKCE migration is complete for iOS and Android. API key rotation scheduled for next week as a deprecation step — old keys will stop working on May 1st.
The team chose TimescaleDB over plain PostgreSQL for the metrics warehouse because we need hypertable partitioning for the 2B+ rows per month of telemetry data.
TimescaleDB deployment uses continuous aggregates for the dashboard queries — raw data retention is 90 days, aggregates kept for 2 years.
We replaced the in-process LRU cache with Redis because cache invalidation across 12 pods was causing stale reads on the product catalog for up to 30 seconds.
Redis cache layer is live with a 5-minute TTL on catalog entries. Cache hit rate jumped from 62% to 94% and stale reads dropped to zero across all pods.
Canary deployments now gate on error rate and p99 latency — if either metric regresses more than 10% during the 15-minute bake window, the rollout auto-reverts.
The canary auto-revert saved us last Thursday — a bad config change spiked p99 from 200ms to 1.2s and the rollout killed itself within 4 minutes.
